text:
tara (sec-eng): Quick heads upplanning a small RBAC change for the private control plane at 02:00 UTC. During staging dry-run saw repeated KMS AccessDenied + same SA token observed from multiple namespaces. Need fast triage before we touch prod.

ben (infra): Can you drop the log lines?

tara (sec-eng): From staging-audit: 
```
2025-01-08T00:12:04Z KMS Request: method=kms.Decrypt result=AccessDenied key=projects/internal/keys/priv-deploy principal=system:serviceaccount:deploy:ci-runner pod=ci-5f9b
2025-01-08T00:12:07Z Auth debug: token=sa-token-zz9 reused_from_ns=[deploy, test, integration]
```

kai (platform): :eyes: That looks like token projection being used incorrectly. Which nodepool image are we on? Older nodes had boundServiceAccountTokenVolume=true disabled in some clusters.

axel (onprem-eng): I've seen this when kubelet token rotation isn't enabled. Could be a stale token hanging around on older nodes. Short term we should block direct egress to KMS and force jobs through the kms-proxy.

ops-bot: ALERT - HIGH - KMS AccessDenied spike detected in staging (rule:kms-token-reuse). Automated correlation: repeated token reuse across ns.

ben (infra): Immediate mitigation options:
- apply a network policy to deny egress from suspect namespaces to external KMS IPs
- cordon older nodepool to force token refresh
- annotate suspect SA and delete secrets to invalidate tokens

tara (sec-eng): Running commands in staging now: 
```bash
kubectl annotate sa ci-runner redwood/security-revoked=true -n deploy
kubectl delete secret ci-runner-token -n deploy || true
# apply temporary netpol (deny egress to kms)
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-kms-egress
  namespace: deploy
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
EOF
```

nora (compliance): Please snapshot the audit logs before any key rotation and push to retention bucket. Need chain-of-custody notes if this hits prod. Tagging compliance.

axel (onprem-eng): For on-prem bastion: adding an immediate iptables rule to block outbound 443 to kms IPs except from the proxy host. Example: 
```bash
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 198.51.100.10 --dport 443 -j REJECT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 198.51.100.11 --dport 443 -j REJECT
# allow proxy host
iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.12 -d 198.51.100.10 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
```

ben (infra): I'll run a dependency scan across infra for that KMS key: `./tools/kms-usage-scan --key=priv-deploy` and post results. If rotation is needed we'll schedule with Hosted/Dedicated teams.

kai (platform): Long term fixes:
- enforce audience-bound tokens (TokenRequest + webhook)
- require workload identity attributes in KMS IAM Conditions (principal set to workload identity)
- tighten SA lifetime on older nodepools / upgrade node images

tara (sec-eng): Running a quick canary: netpol applied and SA annotated at 00:18 UTC. Initial checks: KMS AccessDenied traces dropped to baseline. One integration test job in deploy failed due to missing credential access (expected).

ops-bot: Incident state -> contained (staging). Recommended: do not proceed with prod RBAC change until root cause and key bindings are validated.

nora (compliance): Thanks. Please attach the audit snapshot and the netpol diff to the runbook. We'll escalate if any prod alerts appear.

axel (onprem-eng): CVE-note: a kubelet token-projection CVE affects older images (CVE-2024-XXXX). Plan: upgrade node images this week and enable TokenRequest for all clusters.

ben (infra): Scan results: two test harnesses use the key (non-prod). Scheduling key rotation 2025-01-09 03:30 UTC; will coordinate rollback plan.

kai (platform): I'll prepare an IAM condition template: `request.auth.claims.workload == "projects/_/serviceAccounts/deploy@internal" && request.time < timestamp("2025-01-09T04:00:00Z")` and run it in a dry-run audit.

tara (sec-eng): Postpone tonight's RBAC rollout. We'll reconvene in morning to confirm node upgrades, token audience enforcement, and KMS IAM tightening. Great quick response, team. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: If similar behavior is seen in prod, paging will trigger and this thread will be escalated.

nora (compliance): I'll prepare a discovery questionnaire for the postmortem (who had access, what keys touched, token lifetimes).

ben (infra): Leaving a note: cordoned nodepool at 00:22 UTC; nodes will recycle and tokens should reissue.

tara (sec-eng): Closing loop for now. If anything shows up, ping @nora and @kai and drop logs here.

axel (onprem-eng): Thanks, everyone. We'll follow up with a short playbook to rotate to ephemeral credentials for critical workloads.
